rows:
STATUS
This document closes CHECKLIST 10 at implementation-design level. It converts the locked narrative baseline and the decisions from Checklists 01–09 into a single authoritative game-state model: stable event IDs, enums, counters, sets, dependencies, historical records and postgame restoration state. Later implementation may alter serialization syntax, tooling or presentation, but may not silently change the state meanings or story consequences fixed here.

blocks.text: LOCK SUMMARY

The save stores the smallest authoritative facts and derives convenience conditions from them. Chapters, towns, leaders, Hell circles, NPC arcs and quests use compact state machines instead of contradictory boolean piles. Existing Story Bible scene IDs remain canonical. Historical facts are never overwritten by later restoration: an executed leader remains historically EXECUTED even if revived. Human restoration is separate from Abyssal memorial resurrection and provides exactly five elective uses; Pate and Trade are optional targets, so declining either or both frees uses for leaders Aimon executed. Human memorial entries remain after revival because they record historical death and remembrance.

rows:
CANON SUPERSESSION — HUMAN RESTORATION
The latest approved Checklist 10 decision supersedes the earlier wording in CHECKLIST 09 v1.0 that automatically allocated two of the five human restorations to Pate and Trade. The authoritative rule is now: five total elective human restorations. Pate and Trade each consume one only if the player chooses to restore them. Unused capacity may instead restore eligible executed mortal leaders.

blocks.text: 1. Canon authority and completion boundary
• The Pre-Programming Planning Checklists Reference defines Checklist 10 as the workstream that converts narrative canon into implementation-ready game state.

• The locked Story Bible remains authority for chapter order, authored scene content, existing CHxx-Eyy / CHxx-Oyy IDs, character arcs and narrative causality, except where a later explicit user decision supersedes it.
• Checklist 09 remains authority for SPARE / EXECUTE presentation and human-fate consequences. Checklist 10 owns the final state schema, identifiers and restoration wiring.
• Checklist 07 remains authority for the Abyssal memorial and ten-distinct-species resurrection transaction. Human restoration is not part of that system.
• Checklist 11 owns final species-specific evolution validation; Checklist 10 only defines how story-evolution triggers are stored.
• Checklist 14 owns starter three-life state; Checklist 15 owns Ironman persistence and autosave timing; Checklist 17 owns exact overworld object movement and interaction.
2. Governing implementation principle

rows:
AUTHORITATIVE-STATE RULE
Store the smallest authoritative fact once, then derive every convenience flag from it. Do not save multiple booleans that can contradict one another. Historical choices must remain queryable even when later events change a character’s current condition.

blocks.text: • No visible morality meter. Dialogue may derive counts or patterns from individual leader fates, but the game never stores or displays a single morality score.
• Player-facing names are not save keys. Stable IDs survive localisation, renaming and presentation changes.
• Irreversible story choices and their directly dependent world-state mutations are one logical transaction. Checklist 15 will define the exact disk-write order.
• Append-only history is used where later dialogue must know what happened, not merely what is true now.
3. Naming and identifier conventions

Preserved exactly; E = mandatory, O = optional

blocks.text: • IDs are immutable after shipping. Deleted content leaves the identifier retired rather than reusing it for a different event.
• Display labels, chapter names and NPC names may change without changing stored IDs.
• Implementation may serialize enums numerically, but code and data definitions must expose named constants.

5. Five-use human restoration system

rows:
LOCKED HUMAN RESTORATION RULE
Human restoration is a separate authored postgame/finale system with exactly five total elective uses. It shares no cost, UI, sacrifice rule or transaction with the Abyssal memorial.

blocks.text: • Restoration choices are individual. The player is not forced to spend all five uses in a single menu or to restore Pate and Trade.
• A revived human may leave, retire, wander, serve another role or otherwise live a different life. Revival never silently reinstates former political authority.
• Human memorial entries represent historical death and commemoration, not a list of only those currently dead. They therefore persist after revival.
• The Abyssal memorial remains different: restored Abyssals are removed from the visible Abyssal memorial because that section lists currently dead Abyssals.

blocks.text: 10. Dependency and impossibility rules
• A leader fate cannot be SPARED or EXECUTED before that leader’s authored defeat/surrender resolution point.
• A tracked conquest town cannot enter CONQUERED merely because the leader’s final Abyssal is defeated; the human fate scene must resolve first.
• Leader_fate can never return to UNRESOLVED after commit.
• human_life_state=REVIVED never changes leader_fate from EXECUTED to SPARED.
• An executed leader is eligible for human restoration only while current life state is DEAD and the restoration system is unlocked.
• The human restoration pool can never exceed five successful unique human restorations; the same person cannot consume a second use.
• Pate and Trade are not mandatory restoration targets. Main/postgame state must support both dead, either revived, or both revived.
• Human memorial entries, once authored by historical death, persist after revival.
• Abyssal memorial establishment requires a recorded permanent Abyssal death plus a later Civeton arrival.
• Abyssal resurrection cannot occur through human restoration state, and human restoration cannot invoke the ten-Abyssal sacrifice economy.
• A Warden defeat cannot be recorded unless its battle resolves; a Hell circle cannot be COMPLETE before its required climax.
• Story-evolution triggers, claimed treasures, opened persistent doors and unlocked shortcuts never revert under ordinary play.
• A one-time object ID cannot be claimed/completed twice.
• Chapter N+1 normally cannot become AVAILABLE before the required endpoint of Chapter N, except explicit authored branches/postgame routing.
• Impossible state combinations are development validation errors, not states the runtime silently repairs.
